messages:
Devon: heads-up — I'll be handing off the bridge at 02:00 UTC. quick note: primary is Maria, secondary is Aj for the 02:00-10:00 window.
OncallBot: :rotating_light: paging log: 4 alerts in last 10m for /api/generate latency > 600ms. Triggered by rule: latency-service-95p.
Maria: copying. I’m primary. few things to watch: 95p latency, error spikes in p99, and any queue buildup in worker-pool-3.
Aj: I’ll be secondary but offline for ~30m starting 04:15 UTC for client call. Samir will cover if anything lands then.
Samir: confirmed I’ll be reachable via phone during Aj’s call. phone +1-555-0102.
Devon: quick coverage gaps: early-morning autoscaler cool-downs have caused missed scale-ups in the past — see runbook below. Also watch for the worker restart loop.
Maria: can someone post the runbook links and the minimal commands? don’t want to dig through the wiki mid-incident.
Elena: posting condensed runbook snippets and dashboard links: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-95p  |  https://dashboards.redwood/svc/generate/overview
Elena: quick remedial checklist (short):
- Check queue depth: `kubectl get hpa -n prod worker-pool-3 -o yaml`
- Check pods in CrashLoop: `kubectl describe pod <pod>`
- Check autoscaler events: `gcloud logging read "resource.type=k8s_cluster AND logName=projects/..." --limit 50`
- If scale failure: trigger manual scale: `kubectl scale --replicas=10 deploy/worker-pool-3 -n prod`
Maria: if latency is from long-tail KV hits, enable cache-prefetch toggle: `flags set cache.prefetch=true` (applies per region).
Aj: what about fallback routing? can we route to smaller model to reduce token latency?
Devon: yes — policy is: if p95 > 400ms and cost check passes, route to model-m7-lite. Use: `route apply --from model-m7 --to model-m7-lite --percent=100` (can rollback in 5m).
OncallBot: reminder: when you change routing, annotate the change in the incident bridge: `/incident annotate routing-change model-m7-lite`
Samir: customer impact callout: if error rate > 2% for more than 5m escalate to SEs and set severity=2.
Maria: I’ll monitor error rate and queue depth for the first 20m. Aj — if you’re still on the call at 04:15, ping Samir to take over.
Aj: noted. Samir, I’ll DM the escalation checklist.
Devon: FYI — recent regression we saw last week had a hot-partition in shards: check `kv-shard-metrics` and if you see >90% tail latency, do `kv admin rebalance --shard=hot`.
Elena: adding two quick log grep patterns to find the culprit fast:
```
# find 500s from model runtime
kubectl logs -l app=gateway -n prod --since=10m | grep "500" | head -n 50
# find long model init
kubectl logs -l app=serving -n prod --since=5m | grep "init_time" | awk '$2 > 200'
```
Maria: if manual scaling doesn’t help within 3 minutes, open a P1 with infra and request nodepool resize. Tag infra-oncall.
Samir: adding runbook quicklink: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/scale-and-fallback (one-pager)
Devon: small ops tip — use `bridge notes` to capture any config change and include the git sha of the traffic-shaping manifest. saves time in rollback.
Maria: acknowledged. I’ll also create a short alert-specific watch channel and invite infra-oncall if we need nodepool changes.
Aj: once I’m back, I’ll run a post-shift checklist: ensure any temporary routes or flags are reverted.
Elena: final quick pointer: for any DB-side slowness, check read-replica lag: `pg_stat_replication` and failover only if lag > 120s.
Devon: ok team — thanks. I’m handing off the bridge to you, Maria. ping if anything spikes.
OncallBot: :white_check_mark: handoff recorded: from Devon to Maria at 02:00 UTC. participants: Maria, Aj, Samir, Elena.
